variants: H2 and H2 EDU on the product page, which lists secondary development for the EDU version only. Unitree publishes an H2 Plus on a product page of its own, which this record does not cover.
availability_note: Unitree's product page states a price for the H2 and lists the H2 EDU as contact sales. The shop page carries the same price but shows no add-to-cart control, marks the base variant out of stock, and offers a Contact Sales button as its only route to a price.

hardware.compute: Two PC slots, an Intel Core i5 for platform capabilities and an Intel Core i7 for custom development. The product page's description says a 2070 TOPS chip powers the robot, and a high-power computing module is an accessory, with multiple brands and models available such as Thor.
hardware.sensors: A humanoid binocular camera with a wide field of view, and a voice-interaction array of microphone and high-power speaker. WiFi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2 are listed as present.
hardware.actuation: Low-inertia high-speed internal-rotor permanent magnet synchronous motors on industrial-grade crossed roller bearings, with 31 degrees of freedom in total: six per leg, seven per arm, three at the waist, and two at the head. The page states a maximum arm-joint torque of 120 N·m and leg-joint torque of 360 N·m, an arm payload peaking at about 15 kg and rated at about 7 kg, a standing size of 1820 x 456 x 218 mm, a weight of about 70 kg with battery, a calf-plus-thigh length of 1045 mm and a forearm-plus-upper-arm length of 690 mm, and a body of aircraft-grade aluminium, titanium alloy, and high-strength engineering plastics. A bionic head with facial features and dexterous hands in several models are listed.
hardware.power: A premium lithium battery with low internal resistance, 15 Ah (0.972 kWh) at up to 75.6 V, with about three hours of battery life. A quick-release smart battery and a charger are accessories, and cooling is local air cooling.

developer_access: Unitree's product page lists secondary development for the H2 EDU and points to a secondary development manual. Its unitree_rl_mjlab repository names the H2 among the robots it supports, registers Unitree-H2-Flat and Unitree-H2-Rough velocity-tracking tasks, and documents a Train, Play, Sim2Real workflow that deploys trained policies to physical Unitree robots, worked through on the G1. Its unitree_sdk2 repository ships an h2 example directory with low-level joint commands published on rt/lowcmd for the robot's 31 motors and a high-level locomotion client, and its unitree_ros2 repository ships an h2 example that drives H2 ankle commands with ROS 2 messages.
terms_note: Unitree's SDK, unitree_sdk2, is released under the BSD 3-Clause License. Unitree's terms page has Terms, After-sales Terms, Privacy Policy, Disclaimer, and End User License Agreement tabs; the after-sales tab is the hardware warranty policy, and the licence agreement is offered as a downloadable document rather than as page text. The product page lists an 8-month warranty for the H2 and 12 months for the H2 EDU.
not_verified: The documented policy interfaces are Unitree's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Unitree web page or repository file that Unitree can change at any time.
